heard: Earth pulls the space station with nearly 90% of surface gravity. Most people assume astronauts float weightlessly because Earth's gravity disappears in space. At a normal orbital altitude of 400 kilometers, gravity still measures 8.7 meters per second squared. The sensation of weight does not come from gravity, but from contact forces like floors pushing against your body. Without a supporting force resisting you, apparent weight completely drops to zero. Astronauts appear to float because they and the station accelerate downward at the exact same rate. Immense horizontal speed causes Earth's curved surface to drop away as fast as the spacecraft falls. Weightlessness is never the absence of gravity, but an unending fall around the planet.
